conflicts.issue: Pleuropulmonary blastoma, pulmonary blastoma, carcinosarcoma and myoepithelial carcinoma are WHO lung tumours, three of them in the WHO carcinoma chapters, but ICCC-2017 places them in XIIa3 and XIIa4 at every site. The lung screen refers them to Group XII.
Mesothelioma is ICCC XIIa5 at every site. The pleural screens refer it to Group XII; the benign and uncertain mesothelial tumours (9052/1, 9052/0, 9054/0) are exclusions here.

The tissue-free code 8000/3 (basis 1 or 2) and a histology report of a malignant tumour with no type fall in ICCC XIIb at the lung, pleura, heart and C39, not in Group XI. The subgroup computed at output will be XIIb (registrar question 6).
Lymphomas and histiocytic tumours of the lung refer to Group II. ICCC-2017 holds no range for 9749 Erdheim-Chester disease; the Group II tree carries it.

Lung and pleural sarcomas refer to Group IX. Diffuse lymphangiomatosis carries 9170/3 in the WHO table but ICD-O-3.2's term there is Lymphangiosarcoma; Group IX decides. Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour is 8825/1 (exclusion here); 8825/3 Myofibroblastic sarcoma is Group IX.

ICD-O-3.2 lists Immature teratoma of lung as a Related term at 9080/1 (C34._). Germ cell tumours of the lung or mediastinum belong to the Group X tree; this part offers no germ cell option and the clerk reaches Group X through the router.

The melanoma tree (XId evidence, node mel_site) has no route for melanoma arising in an internal organ such as the lung. The lung and pleural screens send melanoma to mel_site; that node needs an 'another organ' option recording 8720/3 at the stated site.

Thymus and mediastinum part (XIf5) and NUT part: Nicholson 2022 places NUT carcinoma of the thorax under thymic tumours; ICD-O-3.2 lists Intrapulmonary thymoma at 8580/3 with topography C34._; thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumour presents in the mediastinum, lung or pleura. The lung tree codes NUT carcinoma at the lung site; the mediastinum is routed to the thymus tree (next 'thymus_tree').

The deposit options that record 8010/3 at C80.9 change the topography away from the tree's site. ICCC places 8010/3 at C80.9 in XIf11. The node option carries topography_override C80.9; the engine needs to honour it.

data_gaps.need: Paediatric occurrence of the lung carcinomas that remain picker entries: mucinous adenocarcinoma arising in a congenital pulmonary airway malformation, fetal adenocarcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma and the other WHO subtypes.
data_gaps.why: Ozkan 2024 and Chen 2026, added 8 October 2026, report carcinoid tumour, mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, small cell carcinoma, large cell carcinoma and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in children; those are now options on lu_histology. Ozkan 2024 names a congenital pulmonary airway malformation only as a preexisting disease, not the carcinoma that arises in it. Neither paper reports a named adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma subtype, fetal adenocarcinoma, a salivary gland-type carcinoma other than mucoepidermoid carcinoma, or a sarcomatoid carcinoma in a child, so those stay picker entries.
data_gaps.candidate_source: WHO Classification of Tumours, Paediatric Tumours, 5th ed., thoracic chapter; Dishop MK, Kuruvilla S. Primary and metastatic lung tumors in the pediatric population. Arch Pathol Lab Med 2008;132:1079-1103; Rojas Y, et al. Primary malignant pulmonary tumors in children: a review of the National Cancer Data Base. J Pediatr Surg 2015;50:1004-1008.

data_gaps.why: Nicholson 2022 says mitoses per 2 mm2 and necrosis decide, but does not print the cut-offs. The tree relies on the report naming the type; a numeric gate cannot be built without them.
data_gaps.candidate_source: WHO Classification of Tumours, Thoracic Tumours, 5th ed., 2021, lung neuroendocrine neoplasms chapter.

data_gaps.why: The lu_lab screen rests on the registrar's Visser 2023 Table 4 ruling (chromogranin A 8240/3, serotonin 8241/3, ACTH 8158/3). The lung papers name no serum or urine test, so no page supports the screen for the lung.
data_gaps.candidate_source: Caplin ME, et al. Pulmonary neuroendocrine (carcinoid) tumors: European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society expert consensus. Ann Oncol 2015;26:1604-1620.

data_gaps.need: A primary carcinoma entity of the pleura, pericardium or heart.
data_gaps.why: Sauter 2022 and the ICCR mesothelioma dataset name none; the pleural screen offers carcinoma, NOS, the general picker and the deposit routes only.

data_gaps.need: A paediatric source for the two lung options that rest on none: Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3) and melanoma (8720/3).
data_gaps.why: Neither Ozkan 2024 nor Chen 2026 reports a carcinoma, NOS or a melanoma of the lung in a child. Carcinoma, NOS is the fallback code for a report that names no type; melanoma is a route to the melanoma tree. Both stay options as built; the controller decides.

data_gaps.need: The code for a child's report of bronchoalveolar carcinoma or alveolar carcinoma.
data_gaps.why: Ozkan 2024 cites a series of 211 children in which bronchoalveolar carcinoma was 2% of primary lung malignancies, and Chen 2026 names alveolar carcinoma as an epithelial lung tumour of children. Both are retired terms: ICD-O-3.2 holds Bronchiolo-alveolar carcinoma, NOS as an [obs] synonym at 8250/3 Lepidic adenocarcinoma, keeps 8252/3 Bronchiolo-alveolar carcinoma, non-mucinous current, and marks Alveolar carcinoma [obs] at 8251/3. Nicholson 2022 records that bronchioloalveolar carcinoma was defined as a noninvasive tumour, so neither paper reports lepidic adenocarcinoma itself in a child. Lepidic adenocarcinoma (8250/3) stays a picker entry, 8252/3 stays with registrar question 4, and 8251/3 stays off every screen.
data_gaps.candidate_source: Rojas Y, et al. Primary malignant pulmonary tumors in children: a review of the National Cancer Data Base. J Pediatr Surg 2015;50:1004-1008.

data_gaps.need: A screen entry for a mature teratoma of the lung.
data_gaps.why: Chen 2026 reports a mature teratoma of the lung in a child. ICD-O-3.2 codes Mature teratoma, NOS to 9080/0 (Teratoma, benign), and ICCC-2017 holds 9080 at the lung only at behaviour /3 (Xb2), so it is added as an exclusion. Neither lu_histology nor lu_not_malignant offers it, and section 9 of the evidence records that germ cell tumours of the lung reach the Group X tree through the router. The controller decides between an exclusion option on lu_not_malignant and a referral option to Group X.

data_gaps.why: Seven carcinoma and neuroendocrine entries moved from lu_picker to lu_histology on 8 October 2026.
